rules.title: Hardcoded secrets
rules.description: Credentials embedded in source can be copied into source control, logs, build artifacts, and distributed binaries.
rules.detection_guidance: Look for literal values assigned to credential-like names. This is a heuristic; a value may be a placeholder, and credentials under unrelated names may not be found.
rules.recommended_fix: Load secrets from a protected environment variable or secret manager, restrict access, and rotate any credential that may have been exposed.

rules.title: SQL injection
rules.description: SQL injection occurs when data is composed into a query in a way that lets input alter the query's intended structure.
rules.detection_guidance: Trace whether untrusted values are concatenated or interpolated into SQL passed to a database API. Static pattern checks cannot establish the source or full data flow of every value.
rules.vulnerable_example: cursor.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = '" + name + "'")
rules.recommended_fix: Use parameterized queries and pass input values separately from the SQL statement.

source.name: OWASP SQL Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet

rules.title: Command injection
rules.description: Passing untrusted data through a command interpreter can let input change the command that is executed.
rules.detection_guidance: Review shell-enabled process calls and dynamic command construction. Confirm whether attacker-controlled data can reach the command.
rules.recommended_fix: Prefer a library API. Otherwise pass a fixed executable and separate arguments without a shell, and validate each argument against an allowlist.

source.name: OWASP OS Command Injection Defense Cheat Sheet

rules.title: Unsafe deserialization
rules.description: Deserializing attacker-controlled objects can invoke unsafe behavior or construct unexpected object graphs.
rules.detection_guidance: Identify deserialization APIs and establish whether their input can be influenced by an untrusted source. The API name alone does not prove exploitability.
rules.recommended_fix: Avoid executable object formats for untrusted input. Prefer a constrained data format such as JSON and validate it against an explicit schema.

rules.title: Cross-site scripting (XSS)
rules.description: XSS can occur when untrusted content is interpreted as executable markup or script in a user's browser.
rules.detection_guidance: Trace untrusted values into HTML, JavaScript, URL, and template output contexts. Check framework auto-escaping and any explicit safe-markup bypasses.
rules.recommended_fix: Use context-aware output encoding and framework template escaping. Sanitize only when rich HTML is required, using a maintained allowlist sanitizer.

source.name: OWASP Cross Site Scripting Prevention Cheat Sheet

rules.title: Cross-site request forgery (CSRF)
rules.description: CSRF abuses a browser's ambient credentials to trigger an action the authenticated user did not intend.
rules.detection_guidance: Review state-changing browser requests that rely on cookies or other automatically attached credentials, and verify that framework CSRF protections are enabled.
rules.vulnerable_example: A cookie-authenticated state-changing endpoint accepts requests without a CSRF token or equivalent origin protection.
rules.recommended_fix: Use framework CSRF middleware and validated anti-CSRF tokens; configure SameSite cookies and origin checks as defense in depth.

source.name: OWASP Cross-Site Request Forgery Prevention Cheat Sheet

rules.title: Authentication and password handling
rules.description: Weak authentication and unsafe password or session handling can enable account compromise.
rules.detection_guidance: Review password storage, login throttling, recovery flows, session creation and invalidation, and use of maintained identity libraries.
rules.vulnerable_example: Comparing a submitted password directly with a plaintext password stored in a database.
rules.recommended_fix: Use a maintained authentication library and a dedicated adaptive password-hashing function. Protect recovery and session lifecycle flows.

rules.title: Broken access control
rules.description: Missing server-side authorization can allow users to read or modify resources outside their permitted scope.
rules.detection_guidance: Trace resource access and state changes to server-side checks for identity, ownership, role, and policy; UI visibility is not an authorization control.
rules.vulnerable_example: Returning an order by ID without checking that the authenticated user can access it.
rules.recommended_fix: Enforce authorization on every protected operation using the authenticated principal and the resource's ownership or policy.

rules.title: Input validation and sensitive data exposure
rules.description: Unvalidated data and unnecessary exposure or weak protection of sensitive information can cause security and privacy failures.
rules.detection_guidance: Check data at trust boundaries for type, length, range, and format. Review whether sensitive values are minimized, protected in transit and at rest, and excluded from logs and errors.
rules.vulnerable_example: Logging an entire request object that may contain credentials or personal information.
rules.recommended_fix: Validate against an explicit allowlist and schema. Minimize collected data, use maintained cryptographic libraries, and redact sensitive values from logs and responses.

rules.title: Unsafe error handling
rules.description: Detailed internal errors returned to untrusted callers can disclose implementation details or sensitive data.
rules.detection_guidance: Inspect exception responses and logs for stack traces, tokens, personal data, and internal configuration. Preserve useful protected diagnostics for operators.
rules.vulnerable_example: Returning a full exception stack trace in an unauthenticated API response.
rules.recommended_fix: Return a generic, stable error message to callers and log sanitized diagnostic context through access-controlled logging.

rules.title: Maintainability and code smells
rules.description: High complexity, unclear names, dead code, and duplication make behavior harder to verify and changes riskier.
rules.detection_guidance: Use language-aware linters and review control-flow complexity, duplicate logic, naming, and unused declarations. A style warning alone is not evidence of a security vulnerability.
rules.vulnerable_example: Repeated copies of the same authorization or validation logic that can drift over time.
rules.recommended_fix: Prefer focused functions, descriptive names, shared well-tested logic, and removal of truly unused code; verify behavior with tests.
